items.title: Jeffrey Wigand, Who Blew the Whistle on Big Tobacco, Takes a Lot of Calls
items.author: David Streitfeld
items.content: <article>Jeffrey Wigand, who took on Big Tobacco, counsels insiders who think they have a story about wrongdoing. There are quite a few of them.</article>

items.title: Researchers Identify Suspicious Activity on Kalshi and Polymarket Before Times/Siena Poll Release
items.author: Lauren McCarthy and Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>A trader placed well-timed bets on Polymarket and Kalshi in two Senate races. It was unclear if the person had access to inside information or simply made good trades.</article>

items.title: F.A.A. to Phase Out Floppy Disks in Air Traffic Control Towers
items.author: Victor Mather
items.content: <article>Decades after the computer industry moved on, federal officials plan to finally ground the once-vaunted tech relic at the nation’s air traffic control centers.</article>

items.title: Why the Tech Right Lost Big This Week
items.author: Max Read, Erin Griffith, Whitney Jones, Sawyer Roque, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Diane Wong
items.content: <article>“This felt like a decidedly anti-tech election.”</article>

items.title: What Shaped Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s Thinking on A.I.
items.author: Ryan Mac, Kalley Huang, Cade Metz and Georgia Gee
items.content: <article>Some call him a doomer. Others see him as a responsible technologist. Here’s how Dario Amodei’s thinking on artificial intelligence was shaped.</article>

items.title: Microsoft’s Buyout Offer Sets Its Workforce on Edge
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>As Microsoft pours billions into artificial intelligence, the company has offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees. The work force was already on edge.</article>

items.title: Tired of Slow TikToks? This Content Creator Gives You the Ending
items.author: Victor Mather
items.content: <article>Videos on social media often save key details for the end. One content creator, who goes by Heyitsyoon, skips the filler so viewers don’t have to wait.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Pledges to Give Locals More Say in Data Center Projects
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The artificial intelligence company pledged to be more collaborative with the communities where it is building its data centers.</article>

items.title: House G.O.P. Leaders Ask Nvidia’s Huang to Speak in Closed-Door Briefing
items.author: Tripp Mickle
items.content: <article>The New York Times reported last week that Mr. Huang had a close relationship with an executive that U.S. officials determined was funneling information to Chinese intelligence.</article>

items.title: Tech Billionaires Face Tricky Political Waters After Democratic Midterm Sweep
items.author: Eli Tan, Theodore Schleifer and Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>Many donated money to President Trump’s favored causes and became his allies. Now that political alignment may be a liability.</article>

items.title: Google, Meta and TikTok Sue California Over Ban on Features for Kids
items.author: Kate Conger
items.content: <article>Separate lawsuits were filed by Google, Meta and TikTok, which have been battling a flood of claims that their services are addictive.</article>

items.title: Parents Sue Google Over A.I. Safety Risks on School Chromebooks
items.author: Natasha Singer
items.content: <article>A student made plans to end her life after chatting with Google’s artificial intelligence, a new lawsuit claims, amid mounting concerns about online harms to children.</article>

items.title: Amazon Kindle Colorsoft Review: The Single-Task Gadget of Our Times
items.author: Brian X. Chen
items.content: <article>E-book reader sales are soaring as consumers seek technology offering respite from social media and artificial intelligence hype. It’s even better in color.</article>

items.title: Voters Rejected A.I. in the Midterms. Now Comes an Era of Scrutiny.
items.author: Cecilia Kang and Sophia June
items.content: <article>After two years of little A.I. oversight, voters on Tuesday rejected data center projects and swept into office Democratic candidates who promised to regulate the technology.</article>

items.title: Sherrod Brown’s Win in Ohio Is a Rare Loss for Crypto Under Trump
items.author: David McCabe and Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>Fairshake, the major industry super PAC, spent $46 million on ads against the Democrat, Sherrod Brown, who won.</article>

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Set Up ‘War Rooms’ to Fight Disinfo About Midterm Elections
items.author: Steven Lee Myers
items.content: <article>OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday’s elections from efforts to undermine democracy.</article>

items.title: Voting Problems Cause a Surge in Misleading Fraud Claims Online
items.author: Stuart A. Thompson
items.content: <article>Mentions of “cheat,” “steal,” “rig” and similar terms spiked on X this morning as voting began.</article>

items.title: Binance Says Hackers Plotted $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist for Months
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>A report from the cryptocurrency exchange described a monthslong campaign involving fake job interviews that exploited an engineer’s work computer and an internal A.I. tool.</article>

items.title: Are Freezers Being Hacked? Europe and the U.S. Military Investigate.
items.author: Ali Watkins
items.content: <article>A wave of disruptions at grocery stores, which some officials blame on cyberattacks, highlights the vulnerability of supply chains. Shops across Europe were affected again on Monday.</article>

items.title: Apple’s Profit Grows 12% Despite Component Price Worries
items.author: Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The company said iPhone sales remained strong, but warned that the cost of memory chips for its devices was going up.</article>

items.title: Driven by A.I. Boom, Marvell and Lumentum Announce $115 Billion Merger
items.author: Don Clark
items.content: <article>Marvell and Lumentum said they were combining, in a major bet on a technology, known as optical networking, that is increasingly being used in A.I. data centers.</article>

items.title: Inside Anthropic’s Hunt for A.I. Computing Power
items.author: Sri Muppidi and Kalley Huang
items.content: <article>The company went on a deal spree with tech giants, former crypto miners and others to gain computing power to further its artificial intelligence ambitions.</article>

items.title: Deportees Turn to TikTok to Document Life Starting Over
items.author: Isabella Kwai
items.content: <article>On TikTok, men and women sent back after living in the United States are documenting the reality of starting over — and finding an audience.</article>

items.title: Cyril Hilsum, Who Helped Invent Flat-Panel Displays in TVs and iPhones, Has Died at 101
items.author: Michael S. Rosenwald
items.content: <article>The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.</article>

items.title: How Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down
items.author: David Yaffe-Bellany
items.content: <article>A war room. A global conference call. A founder who live-posted about the largest crypto heist in history. Inside a frantic 24 hours at the world’s biggest crypto exchange.</article>
